items.title: "Digital Society And Ethical Issues: Challenges, Opportunities And The Future Of Responsible Digital Transformation"
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of digital technologies has transformed modern society in almost every sphere of human life. The growth of the internet, smartphones, social media, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data, digital payments, e-commerce, and online education has created what is commonly described as a digital society. Digital technologies have improved communication, access to information, education, healthcare, business, public administration, and economic participation. At the same time, the increasing dependence on digital systems has created significant ethical challenges relating to privacy, data protection, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, misinformation, digital inequality, online harassment, intellectual property, surveillance, and the responsible use of emerging technologies.

items.title: A brief study of Tribal Brick Workers: Special reference of Thane district
items.abstract: Abstract- Brick’s manufacturing is an important industry in India. Bricks are very important raw material required in construction. Thousands of construction projects are ongoing in Mumbai Economic zone and thane district. Bricks manufacturers in thane district are primary suppliers of bricks to these construction sites. Large number of tribal communities from thane district are engaged as bricks worker in Bricks manufacturing Industry. These Tribal Brick workers play an important role in the construction industry, providing the foundation for buildings, homes, and other infrastructure projects. Despite their significant contribution, they have very challenging lives. Harsh physical labour, prolong working hours, and limited resources is an everyday issue for these workers. These tribal workers have lack of formal education, which limits their employment opportunities outside the brick industry. These workers Often employed on a seasonal basis, with very low wages, long working hours, and. Due to illiteracy and poor economic condition times, they often exploited by their owners. This article will focus on the working and living conditions of brick workers in the Thane district. This research aims to understand the socio-economic status and problems, occupational health issues, and the impact of their work environment on their overall well-being of Tribal Bricks Wokers. This paper is going to focus on the problems and possible remedies to address the various issues of Tribal Brick Workers. This research will be helpful to the broader discourse on informal labours problems and provides a foundation for policymakers and social organizations to address the challenges faced by brick workers.

items.title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Phishing Website Detection Using URL and Host-Based Features with Leakage-Resistant Stacking
items.abstract: One of the biggest cybersecurity dangers is phishing websites, which trick users into providing confidential information through fake interfaces. Traditional detection solutions, such as black-list and rule-based methods, are no longer effective against emerging attacks. To address the limitations of existing approaches, this study proposes an integrated machine learning system based on URL and host-based characteristics, designed to improve generalization and avoid data leakage. The proposed model uses two branches, each training a separate classifier on a different feature set (URL and host). These branches are combined using a leakage-resistant Out-Of-Fold (OOF) stacking mechanism that derives meta-features from unseen data. In addition, interaction-based meta-features are added to further boost predictive power. The UCI Phishing Websites Dataset, containing 11,055 instances and 17 selected features, was used to evaluate the model. The experimental results validate the proposed hybrid model, which achieves an accuracy of 92.67\% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9788, outperforming the single feature-based models. Cross-validation shows good generalization with low variance. Feature importance analysis shows that the interaction-based meta-features are highly influential in improving classification accuracy. The model achieves a strong balance between performance, computational efficiency, and interpretability compared with contemporary approaches. Its leakage-resistant design enables unbiased evaluation and real-world applicability in cybersecurity. This work contributes to phishing detection research through hybrid ensemble learning with an emphasis on methodological rigor and extensive performance evaluation.

items.title: A Study of Web 1.0 To Web 4.0: Evolution, Technologies, Applications and Future Directions
items.abstract: Abstract The World Wide Web has evolved from a predominantly static information environment into an increasingly interactive, semantic, distributed and intelligent digital ecosystem. The earlier study on Web 1.0 to Web 3.0 described the transition from the read-only web to the read-write social web and then toward the semantic web. This revised study extends that framework to Web 4.0 and examines the technological and conceptual changes across the four stages. Web 1.0 is characterized by static pages, one-way information delivery and limited user participation; Web 2.0 emphasizes interaction, user-generated content, social networking and web applications; Web 3.0 is associated with semantic interoperability, decentralized architectures, data ownership and intelligent processing; and Web 4.0 is increasingly discussed as an intelligent or symbiotic web in which artificial intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), cloud/edge computing, augmented and virtual reality, machine-to-machine communication and autonomous agents can interact with people and each other. The literature does not provide one universally accepted definition of Web 4.0, so this paper treats it as an emerging research and technology paradigm rather than a fixed technical standard. The study also discusses implications for libraries and information services, including intelligent discovery, personalized services, virtual assistance, semantic knowledge organization and human-machine collaboration. The paper concludes that the movement from Web 1.0 to Web 4.0 represents a shift from information access toward participation, meaning, intelligence and increasingly symbiotic interaction.

items.title: A STUDY ON AI ADOPTION AND EMPLOYEE SATISFACTION IN THE INDIAN HEALTHCARE SECTOR
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare systems is rapidly increasing in India, with the market estimated to grow from $0.83 billion in 2023 to $17.75 billion by 2032. Employee satisfaction remains a major concern that relevant studies in the healthcare sector have yet to address. This article explores how AI integration is affecting employee satisfaction in India’s healthcare industry. The healthcare industry faces a 60% shortage of digital skills; 47% of Indian healthcare workers are not digitally literate, and only 34% of organizations are advancing toward piloting AI projects, despite 86% having adopted AI. Implementation challenges include limited technical expertise among clinicians, the psychological burden of increased monitoring, poor rural infrastructure, data privacy concerns, and workforce constraints. For AI to succeed, it must be presented as a supplement to workers, not a replacement. This shift should include targeted training to address digital literacy gaps, governance that incorporates clinician input in system design, and ongoing staffing support. Existing evidence suggests that AI adoption may be associated with burnout and reduced employee satisfaction when it is not coupled with these integrated efforts. Beyond technical expertise, research highlights human-centered design, thorough training for healthcare professionals, and maintaining autonomy as key drivers of effective AI integration in healthcare in India. To benefit from AI, healthcare facilities in India must adopt modern technology. They must also prioritize staff well-being.

items.title: A VR-Based Multimodal System for Assessing Presentation Integrity and Character Formation in Higher Education
items.abstract: Background. Artificial intelligence (AI) integration in online presentation assessment has expanded rapidly; however, existing facial emotion recognition systems in education remain largely focused on surveillance and behavioral monitoring, with limited validation against human judgment and insufficient attention to ethical and character-development dimensions. Purpose. This study aimed to develop and validate a virtual reality (VR)-based multimodal assessment framework for evaluating presentation integrity among higher education students. Method. A design science research approach was employed involving 64 students from two parallel classes (A1, n = 33; A2, n = 31) at a university in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Data from expert validation, technical performance evaluation, NASA-TLX, System Usability Scale, and lecturer assessments were analyzed using content validity analysis with modified kappa, classification metrics, Bland-Altman agreement analysis, and descriptive statistics. Novelty. This study introduces a human-centered AI-VR assessment approach that integrates facial emotion recognition, gaze detection, and cognitive load measurement into a reflective Presentation Integrity Index. Unlike conventional AI-based monitoring systems that generate binary judgments, the proposed framework emphasizes ethical interpretation by combining affective, behavioral, and cognitive indicators to support formative character-based assessment. Results. The framework demonstrated satisfactory content validity (S-CVI/Ave = 0.83), although refinement of several indicators was required. Emotion and gaze modules achieved accuracy levels of 85.3% and 89.0%, respectively. The Presentation Integrity Index showed 93.8% agreement with lecturer assessments, moderate cognitive load (NASA-TLX = 46.7), and good usability (SUS = 76.4). Conclusion. The proposed AI-VR framework provides an ethical and reflective approach for character-based presentation assessment while requiring broader validation involving multiple evaluators and diverse educational contexts.

items.title: Advertising the Sustainable Future: AI, Immersive Media and Behaviour Change for Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract Viksit Bharat 2047 will not be achieved through infrastructure and technology alone. Much of the change will be visible in ordinary routines: the way electricity and water are used at home, the way waste is handled, the products people choose, and the willingness of communities to take part in local environmental efforts. Advertising is relevant here because it already knows how to reach large audiences, tell memorable stories and influence everyday choices. Advertising itself is changing quickly. Artificial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), spatial computing and algorithmic personalisation are giving audiences more interactive forms of communication. This paper considers what these developments could mean for sustainability campaigns. The main concern is a familiar one: people may genuinely care about environmental issues and still struggle to turn that concern into consistent behaviour. The discussion draws on secondary material relating to the IndiaAI Mission, NITI Aayog policy directions, Sustainable Development Goal 12 and media-effects research. On this basis, the paper develops the AI-Immersive Sustainable Advertising Behaviour Model (AISABM). It brings together five connected ideas: context-sensitive communication, immersive experience, trustworthy information, a simple route to action, and feedback based on observable behaviour. Technology can also create a new divide if access is taken for granted. High-end VR is unlikely to be equally available to everyone, whereas radio, podcasts, smartphones and lightweight AR applications can travel much further. This is why the paper does not present immersive media as a replacement for older channels. It argues for a combination of both. items.title: AI and Digital Economy: Pathway to Sustainable Development and Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Digital Economy are increasingly shaping India's economic transformation. Their applications in agriculture, manufacturing, services, banking, education, healthcare, governance and entrepreneurship have the potential to improve productivity, reduce transaction costs, expand access to services and strengthen innovation. This study examines the economic role of AI and digitalisation with particular reference to sustainable development and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The study is based on secondary data and follows a descriptive and analytical approach. Official statistics on internet connectivity, digital payments and the IndiaAI Mission are used to provide a quantitative dimension to the analysis. The evidence shows rapid expansion of India's digital ecosystem: internet subscribers reached 1,028.61 million by December 2025, while rural internet subscribers stood at 407.69 million in March 2025. UPI processed 22,716.07 million transactions worth ₹28,92,138.67 crore in June 2026. The IndiaAI Mission, approved with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore, has expanded compute capacity beyond its initial 10,000-GPU target. The study concludes that AI and digitalisation can support productivity, financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, sustainable resource use and public-service delivery. However, digital inequality, skill gaps, data privacy, cybersecurity, employment restructuring and environmental costs require policy attention. Inclusive infrastructure, human-capital development, responsible AI and sustainable digital practices are therefore essential for Viksit Bharat 2047.

items.title: AI and Digital Public Infrastructure: Building the Foundations of Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India's journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a transformation that combines technological advancement with inclusive and sustainable economic development. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) have emerged as two important pillars of this transformation. While DPI provides the digital foundations for identity, payments, data exchange, and access to public and private services, AI can add intelligence, automation, personalization, and predictive capabilities to these systems. Together, they can significantly improve governance, healthcare, education, agriculture, financial inclusion, digital commerce, and public service delivery. This paper examines the role of AI-enabled Digital Public Infrastructure in building a developed India by 2047. It explores opportunities, challenges, ethical considerations, and the need for responsible and inclusive AI adoption. The paper argues that India's competitive advantage will depend not merely on technological adoption but on developing trusted, accessible, secure, multilingual, and citizen-centric digital ecosystems. Strengthening digital skills, cybersecurity, data governance, research and innovation, and public-private partnerships will be essential for realizing this vision. AI combined with DPI can become a powerful foundation for inclusive prosperity, innovation, and sustainable development in Viksit Bharat.

items.title: AI and Responsible Innovation: Technology, Society and Governance in the Technorapid Age for Viksit Bharat 2047.
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is getting integrated into the day-to-day life of every human being. This fast-changing technology is transforming traditional technology, society and governance at a rapid pace. This paper explores the emerging Technorapid Age, where technological change may move faster than the ability of individuals, institutions and governance systems to adapt. It focuses on Responsible Innovation as a methodology to manage this growing gap. It proposes that AI development should not be measured only by technological progress. It should also consider human well-being, social inclusion, ethical responsibility and effective governance. It examines the relationship between AI, technology and society. It highlights the need for human adaptability, accountability and responsible decision-making. The author proposes that Responsible Innovation can help create an equilibrium between technological acceleration and human adaptive capacity. The paper directly connects with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. India needs technological development that is innovative, inclusive, ethical and sustainable. Technology should support human dignity, social well-being and the needs of future generations. The research concludes that achieving Viksit Bharat 2047 requires comprehensive and responsible AI technologies. These innovations should benefit all sections of society (सर्वजन हिताय, सर्वजन सुखाय) and ensure that people are skilled and supported to handle challenges of the Technorapid Age.

items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming a major driver of India's digital transformation. It is expected to impact governance, education, healthcare, finance, employment and everyday life as India moves towards the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. However, this rapid development and adoption of technology also creates a growing gap between technological progress and the ability of individuals and society to adapt. This paper describes this condition as Technorapid, an accelerating pace of technological change that can exceed human, social, institutional and ethical adaptive capacity. The paper proposes that digital transformation should not remain confined to policies and institutional documents. Its success should ultimately be visible on the ground, in the lived experience of its citizens. AI-driven development needs to be evaluated through its ability to improve access, dignity, inclusion, education, employment and quality of life. This paper explores Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the principle that the world is one family, as a philosophical foundation for a human-centered approach to AI ethics. It argues that India's technological progress should be complemented by human adaptation, ethical governance and mechanisms that ensure that the benefits of AI reach diverse sections of society. The paper concludes that the true measure of Viksit Bharat @2047 should not be how advanced India's technologies become, but how meaningfully those technologies improve human live and national progress

items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence is increasingly being explored as a tool for accelerating progress toward sustainable development. AI can analyse large datasets, identify patterns, forecast events, optimise systems and support decision-making across agriculture, energy, water, healthcare, education, cities, industry and environmental management. Recent research shows that AI-for-SDG research is expanding rapidly, while also revealing gaps in social inclusion, governance and assessment of AI’s own environmental footprint. This project examines the major opportunities for AI-enabled sustainable development, including smart agriculture, renewable-energy optimisation, climate and disaster forecasting, intelligent waste management, sustainable cities, healthcare and education. It also discusses innovation pathways such as machine learning, computer vision, remote sensing, generative AI, digital twins and edge AI. The study emphasises that technological capability alone is insufficient: responsible AI requires reliable data, transparency, privacy, human oversight, equitable access, energy-efficient computing and lifecycle environmental assessment.

items.title: AI Generated Literature and Changing Concepts of Authorship
items.abstract: Abstract: The present research paper deals with AI generated literature and changing concepts of authorship in the period where AI has replaced every sphere of human life. The emergence of generative artificial intelligence has altered assumptions about literary text as the production of human creativity because AI is able to produce poems, stories, essays and other literary forms in response to the simple prompts. As a result, the conventional distinctions between author and reader have become more complicated now. However, the developments questioning the role of authorship into literary studies are not new; rather 20th century literary theory has already challenged the idea of the author as the sole creator of textual meaning. Roland Barthes’ The Death of Author, Michel Foucault’s What Is an Author, T. S. Eliot’s theory of impersonality and W. K. Wimsatt and Monroe Beardsley’s critique pertaining to intentional fallacy displaced the image of the author and demonstrated that literary meaning is produced through language and discourse without considering the intentions of an author. Generative AI further intensifies these theoretical questions by introducing non-human agents into the process of textual production. Thus, the present paper attempts to put forth the role of AI in production of literary text within the frameworks of theories mentioned above.

items.title: AI Use and Learning Outcomes Among Undergraduate Students: The Mediating Role of Learning Motivation, Locus of Control, and Learning Preferences
items.abstract: Background. The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has created new opportunities for personalized learning, although its contribution to student achievement remains theoretically and empirically contested. Purpose. This study examined the direct and indirect effects of AI use on conceptual understanding and problem-solving ability through learning motivation, locus of control, and learning preferences. Method. A quantitative explanatory design was employed with 88 pre-service teachers enrolled in an Instructional Media course at a teacher education institution in Central Java, Indonesia. Data were collected using validated questionnaires and cognitive assessments. Preliminary analyses were conducted using SPSS, while the measurement and structural models were evaluated through PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Novelty. This study simultaneously tested three psychological and learning-related mediators within a single structural model, thereby extending previous research that primarily examined the direct relationship between AI use and academic performance. Results. AI use significantly predicted learning motivation and locus of control but did not significantly influence learning preferences. Learning motivation significantly predicted learning outcomes and mediated the relationship between AI use and learning outcomes. In contrast, locus of control and learning preferences showed no significant mediating effects. The direct effect of AI use on learning outcomes was also nonsignificant. Conclusion. AI contributes to student learning primarily by strengthening learning motivation rather than through direct technological exposure. Effective AI integration should therefore emphasize reflective, autonomous, and cognitively engaging learning activities.

items.title: AI-Assisted Integration of Midgut Digestive Enzymes and Gut Microbiota in Samia ricini: A Predictive Framework for Sustainable Eri-Silk Production
items.abstract: Abstract The eri silkworm, Samia ricini (Lepidoptera: Saturniidae), is an economically important polyphagous silk-producing insect whose productivity is influenced by host-plant quality, digestive physiology, larval development and associated gut microorganisms. The midgut represents a major interface between dietary nutrients and physiological utilization, while the resident microbial community may contribute to nutrient transformation and host adaptation. Although previous studies have independently investigated digestive enzymes, host-plant effects and gut microbial diversity in S. ricini, an integrated predictive framework combining biochemical, microbiome and production variables remains comparatively underdeveloped. The present study proposes an AI-assisted framework for integrating midgut digestive enzyme activity, gut microbiota and larval/cocoon traits in S. ricini. Three host-plant diets—Ricinus communis, Ailanthus altissima and Manihot esculenta—are considered within the proposed experimental framework. Digestive activities of α-amylase, protease, lipase and cellulase are proposed to be evaluated together with 16S rRNA-based bacterial community profiling. Larval growth, survival, cocoon weight, shell weight and shell percentage are incorporated as production-related variables. Statistical approaches including ANOVA, correlation analysis, diversity analysis and PERMANOVA are combined with machine-learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost and Support Vector Regression. For methodological demonstration, a simulated dataset was constructed using biologically plausible ranges rather than experimental observations. The simulated analysis illustrates how integrated biochemical and microbial variables can be used to predict larval and cocoon performance and how SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence can identify influential predictors. The framework suggests that microbiome–enzyme interactions may provide useful candidate biomarkers for future validation. However, simulated findings should not be interpreted as empirical evidence. The proposed framework provides a basis for future experimental studies aimed at microbiome-informed feeding, precision rearing and sustainable eri-silk production.

items.title: AI-Driven Development of Smart Chemical Sensors for Rapid Detection of Environmental Pollution
items.abstract: Abstract Environmental pollution is a complex and continuously evolving problem that requires rapid, sensitive and decentralized analytical technologies. Conventional analytical techniques such as atomic absorption spectrometry, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, gas chromatography and high-performance liquid chromatography provide high analytical performance but generally require sophisticated instrumentation, laboratory infrastructure, sample preparation and trained personnel. Smart chemical sensors offer an attractive alternative because they can provide rapid measurements with portable and potentially low-cost instrumentation. However, environmental samples contain multiple interfering species, and sensor responses may be nonlinear, unstable or affected by temperature, pH, humidity and sensor ageing. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), provides new opportunities to overcome these limitations by extracting complex patterns from chemical-sensor responses and converting them into qualitative or quantitative information. This paper reviews the development of AI-driven smart chemical sensors for rapid environmental pollution detection, with emphasis on electrochemical sensors, gas-sensor arrays, optical sensors and nanomaterial-based sensing platforms. The application of machine-learning approaches including principal component analysis, support-vector machines, artificial neural networks, random forests and deep-learning models for signal processing, classification, quantification and sensor-drift compensation is discussed. Recent studies demonstrate the integration of deep learning, electrochemical sensing and Internet-of-Things technology for simultaneous detection of heavy metals in water. The paper also proposes an integrated framework combining chemical recognition, signal transduction, AI-based data interpretation, wireless communication and environmental decision support. Major challenges, including limited datasets, matrix effects, sensor drift, model interpretability and field validation, are discussed. AI-enabled chemical sensors have considerable potential to transform environmental monitoring from periodic laboratory analysis toward rapid, portable and intelligent pollution surveillance.

items.title: AI-Driven Green Chemistry for Sustainable Development: A Comprehensive Review Towards Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract The escalating global demand for chemicals, materials, and energy has intensified concerns regarding resource depletion, hazardous waste generation, energy consumption, and environmental pollution. Green chemistry provides a sustainable paradigm by minimizing waste, reducing hazardous substances, improving energy efficiency, and promoting renewable resources. However, developing greener chemical processes traditionally requires extensive experimentation and optimization. Artificial intelligence (AI)—particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning, and predictive modeling—offers transformative opportunities to accelerate this transition. AI enables reaction prediction and optimization, catalyst discovery, green solvent selection, sustainable material design, toxicity prediction, waste minimization, and environmental monitoring by analyzing large chemical datasets and identifying relationships recognized through conventional approaches. Integration of AI with automation and advanced analytical techniques further enables faster, more efficient chemical research. This review discusses major applications of AI in green chemistry, emphasizing sustainable synthesis, catalysis, solvents, materials, waste management, energy technologies, and analytical chemistry. We address challenges associated with data quality, model interpretability, experimental validation, computational energy consumption, and industrial scale-up. Finally, we examine the potential of AI-driven green chemistry to support sustainable manufacturing, circular economy, resource efficiency, and technological innovation in India within the context of Viksit Bharat @2047. We conclude that integrating chemical expertise with AI provides a powerful pathway toward cleaner, safer, and more sustainable chemical technologies.

items.title: AI-Driven Precision Agriculture and Crop Resilience: Integrating Artificial Intelligence, IoT and Remote Sensing for Climate-Resilient Indian Agriculture: A Vision for Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract Agriculture is central to India's economic development, food security, rural employment, and the achievement of the Viksit Bharat@2047 vision. However, Indian agriculture faces increasingly complex challenges, including climate variability, water scarcity, soil degradation, pest and disease outbreaks, fragmented landholdings, market uncertainty, and unequal access to agricultural knowledge. These challenges require a transition from conventional, input-intensive agriculture towards data-driven, resource-efficient, climate-resilient and farmer-centric production systems. Agriculture in India is increasingly affected by climate variability, water scarcity, soil degradation, pest and disease outbreaks, and unpredictable weather conditions. These challenges threaten crop productivity and food security, particularly among small and marginal farmers. Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, and machine learning offer new opportunities to transform conventional agricultural practices into data-driven precision agriculture systems. This paper presents a conceptual framework for AI-driven precision agriculture aimed at improving crop resilience under changing climatic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI), combined with precision agriculture, Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, satellite imagery, drones, machine learning, robotics and digital public infrastructure, offers significant opportunities to transform Indian agriculture. AI can support crop and yield prediction, disease and pest identification, weather-based advisories, irrigation optimisation, soil management, crop insurance, market intelligence and early-warning systems. The paper also discusses challenges related to digital inclusion, data governance, affordability, AI reliability, farmer skills, privacy and institutional coordination. It argues that India's objective should not simply be the digitisation of agriculture, but the creation of an intelligent, inclusive and resilient agricultural ecosystem in which technology augments farmer knowledge and decision-making. By 2047, India can aspire to establish globally competitive agriculture that produces more with fewer resources, withstands climate shocks, generates higher and more stable farm incomes, and ensures sustainable food and nutritional security.

items.title: AI-Driven Workplace Surveillance and Employee Privacy: A Labour Law Perspective
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the modern workplace. Employers are increasingly using AI-enabled technologies to monitor attendance, productivity, communication, location, performance, behaviour and emotional responses of employees. While such technologies can offer advantages in terms of organisational efficiency, prevention of misconduct and management of large workforces, they also raise serious concerns over employee privacy, autonomy, dignity and labour rights. Traditional workplace monitoring was generally limited to physical observation, attendance registers and conventional electronic monitoring. AI has enabled wider collection of employee data, which is subsequently evaluated using automated systems. This research explores the relationship between AI-driven workplace surveillance and employee privacy rights, with reference to the Indian legal framework. It examines the challenges created by continuous monitoring, algorithmic decision-making, biometric surveillance, productivity tracking and employee profiling. The study argues that workplace surveillance should not be viewed solely as a question of managerial authority but should be addressed as a labour-rights and fundamental-rights issue. A balanced regulatory approach is therefore crucial to ensure that legitimate business interests do not override employee privacy and dignity. The research concludes with recommendations for transparency, proportionality, informed notice, data minimisation, human oversight and effective grievance mechanisms.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Performance Appraisal Systems: Assessing the Interplay Between Machine Feedback, Employee Motivation, and Career Mobility
items.abstract: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into performance appraisal systems has fundamentally transformed how organizations evaluate, reward, and guide talent. This paper examines the complex interplay between automated machine feedback, employee intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, and long-term career mobility within modern corporate structures. Traditional performance reviews, historically plagued by manager bias, infrequent feedback cycles, and administrative lag, are increasingly being replaced by real-time, algorithmic evaluation tools that continuously monitor productivity, communication patterns, and milestone attainment. While these advanced systems offer unprecedented objectivity, data granularity, and operational efficiency, they simultaneously introduce critical psychological and structural challenges for the workforce. The research investigates how algorithmic oversight impacts employee motivation, exploring the fine line between constructive data-driven guidance and dehumanizing surveillance. When machine feedback is perceived as opaque, overly punitive, or devoid of contextual empathy, it can trigger algorithmic anxiety, disengagement, and strategic gaming of metrics. Conversely, when integrated transparently, AI-driven insights can empower employees with actionable developmental pathways, aligning daily performance with overarching career trajectories. The study further analyzes the implications of automated career mobility, evaluating how machine-generated talent mapping influences promotions, skill-gap identification, and succession planning. It highlights the risk of algorithmic bias reinforcing historical inequities, thereby restricting advancement opportunities for diverse employee segments if human oversight is absent. Methodologically, this paper synthesizes contemporary organizational psychology literature with a comparative evaluation of organizations deploying AI-augmented human resource management systems. The analytical framework correlates the frequency and framing of machine feedback with metrics of employee retention, morale, and promotional velocity. The findings suggest that optimal performance outcomes are achieved not through pure automation, but through a hybrid model where AI serves as an objective diagnostic tool that amplifies—rather than replaces—human managerial mentorship and empathy. Ultimately, this study provides human resource leaders and technologists with a strategic framework for designing ethical, motivation-enhancing appraisal architectures that foster sustainable career growth and organizational agility.

items.title: AI-Generated Review Summaries And Consumer Purchase Decisions: A Conceptual Framework For Indian Gen Z Consumers
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is changing how consumers search for, evaluate and use information in digital marketplaces. One emerging application is the use of AI-generated review summaries, which condense large volumes of online consumer reviews into concise statements about product strengths, weaknesses and frequently mentioned attributes. Such summaries can reduce information overload and improve search efficiency, but they also raise concerns regarding credibility, transparency, objectivity, selective omission and consumer reliance on machine-generated interpretations of peer opinions. This study examines AI-generated review summaries and their potential influence on purchase decisions among Indian Gen Z consumers. The study is primarily secondary-research-led and synthesises recent literature on AI-mediated electronic word-of-mouth, review credibility, transparency, trust and perceived diagnosticity. To complement the secondary evidence, an exploratory primary survey of 120 respondents collected through Google Forms is incorporated as an empirical component. The study adopts the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) perspective and signalling theory to structure the relationships among perceived transparency, perceived usefulness, perceived objectivity, consumer trust, perceived diagnosticity and purchase intention. The paper proposes that trust and diagnosticity function as important mechanisms through which characteristics of AI-generated review summaries can influence purchase intention. The empirical component is designed to provide descriptive and exploratory evidence rather than to replace the broader secondary research base. Statistical analysis includes respondent profiling, descriptive statistics, reliability assessment, correlation analysis and appropriate hypothesis testing, subject to the structure of the 120-response dataset. The study contributes to understanding how AI-mediated review information can support consumer decision-making while highlighting the importance of transparency, balanced representation and access to original reviews.

items.abstract: Abstract India's transition toward a renewable energy-led economy faces critical challenges in grid stability, demand forecasting, and efficient integration of intermittent power sources such as solar and wind. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to overcoming these constraints, enabling predictive load forecasting, real-time fault detection, and autonomous demand-response management across smart grid. Grid Mission, the IndiaAI Mission, and NITI Aayog's National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence. It further examines barriers to scale, including high implementation costs, inconsistent data interoperability across state utilities, cybersecurity vulnerabilities in AI-integrated grid systems, and the skills gap in AI-energy hybrid expertise. Through a review-based analytical framework, the paper proposes an integrated model aligning AI-enabled smart grid deployment with SDG-7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG-13 (Climate Action) within India's Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. The findings suggest that AI-optimized energy systems, if scaled with supportive policy and skilled workforce development, can position India as a global leader in sustainable, technology-driven energy infrastructure.

items.title: Algorithmic Oversight: Caremark's Fiduciary Framework Applied to Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence now drives core corporate decision, such as loan approvals and hiring screens, yet corporate boards have largely treated its governance as a management-level policy questions rather than a fiduciary obligation. This paper argues that this framing is mistaken, using Delaware's Caremark doctrine, as refined by Marchand v. Barnhill, In re Boeing, and In re McDonald's. The relevant cases already impose an enforceable duty on boards to actively oversee mission algorithmic systems, and by applying Marchand's mission-critical standard, this paper demonstrates that AI performs core business functions that expose companies to anti-discrimination, consumer protection, and securities liability. The paper also identifies a structural problem that existing doctrine has not confronted: unlike the legible red flags at issue in Caremark, Boeing, and Clovis Oncology, AI systems generate outputs without human-readable explanations, allowing boards to receive clean compliance reports from systems that are producing unlawful outcomes. This "black box problem" requires reestablishing what good-faith oversight demands and when the underlying risk bypasses traditional reporting structures. Drawing on In re SolarWinds and the officer liability extension in McDonald's, this paper proposes a scalable framework for reasonable AI oversight, including board-level AI audit committees, a Chief AI Officer role with reporting duties to the General Counsel and CEO, mandatory governance disclosure, and a safe harbor for compliance. Ultimately, this paper challenges that the doctrinal tools to govern AI already exist within Delaware law, and all that remains is for boards to act before litigation forces the question.

items.title: An Integrated Community Engagement & Project Management System (Icepms) A Single-Window Digital Ecosystem for Research & Development in Higher Education Institutions in India
items.abstract: Abstract India's higher education system has never lacked policy mandates for community engagement. What it has consistently lacked is a working mechanism to connect community-identified problems with academic institutions positioned to address them. This paper proposes the Integrated Community Engagement & Project Management System (ICEPMS) — a single-window digital ecosystem that bridges this gap by linking community demand directly to higher education delivery. The paper develops a five-stakeholder conceptual model through systematic analysis of national policy documents, international frameworks, and established scholarship on community-based participatory research (CBPR) and service-learning. The proposed system enables citizens, Gram Panchayat members, NGOs, and journalists to report local problems digitally; allows administrators to convert those problems into credit-mapped academic topics; enables colleges and students to execute Community Engagement Projects; records performance transparently; and facilitates funding from CSR departments and government officers based on verifiable institutional performance. The paper discusses the role of artificial intelligence as a supportive accelerator within the system. ICEPMS aligns with the mandates of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the UGC Guidelines for Fostering Social Responsibility and Community Engagement in Higher Education Institutions in India 2.0 (2022), and institutional Community Engagement Project frameworks. By providing operational infrastructure for existing policy intent, the paper contributes a practical framework for community engagement in Indian higher education.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics Teaching and Learning: Opportunities, Challenges and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing mathematics education through personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated feedback, assessment support, and teacher assistance. AI-enabled systems can adapt tasks to learners’ needs, provide immediate feedback, generate practice questions, and help identify misconceptions. Recent reviews suggest that adaptive platforms, intelligent tutoring systems, and generative-AI tools can support engagement, self-paced learning, conceptual understanding, and mathematical problem-solving when used under effective teacher guidance.link.springer+1 However, AI is not a replacement for mathematics teachers. Concerns remain about inaccurate AI-generated solutions, student overdependence, privacy risks, unequal access to devices and internet connectivity, algorithmic bias, and limited teacher preparedness. Evidence also remains mixed, particularly because many studies are short-term and report limited standardized measures of learning impact. This paper reviews the opportunities and challenges of AI in mathematics teaching and learning and proposes a Human–AI Collaborative Framework for responsible, equitable, and pedagogically meaningful implementation.frontiersin+1

items.title: Artificial Intelligence And future of Library and Information Services: A conceptual Perspective
items.abstract: Abstract In the era of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the field of Library and Information Science is evolving rapidly with the introduction of new paradigms in information management, information discovery, and service delivery. This is a conceptual paper that analyses the role of AI and its future implications on the library and information services. It examines key AI technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, chatbots, robotics, AI-powered discovery services, personalized information services and generative AI, and explores how these are being used in modern libraries. This paper emphasises the benefits of these technologies in information retrieval, automating repetitive library functions, delivering personalized services to users, facilitating research activities, and engaging users. It also looks at how technology is evolving like smart libraries and AI-driven information services. Meanwhile, the paper covers important challenges that must be addressed in the context of the adoption of AI, such as privacy, data security, algorithmic bias, misinformation, copyright, ethical issues, technological costs, and technical skills. The evolving nature of the role of LIS professionals and the skills needed to collaborate with emerging AI technologies are given special attention. The paper proposes that AI is not the end of librarians but an enabler and a supportive tool for librarians. By combining AI with professional knowledge, ethical considerations, and human-centred services, libraries can become smarter, more efficient, user-friendly, and responsive to user needs. The study highlights the need for responsible use of AI, ongoing professional growth, and collaboration between technology and human skills to shape the future of library services. items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Higher Education under NEP 2020: A Competency-Based Framework for Achieving Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract AI and ML are rapidly changing higher education by redefining teaching, learning, research, evaluation, and institutional governance. India's National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 envisions a transdisciplinary, technology-enabled, learner-centric, and innovation-driven education system that produces globally competent graduates who can contribute to Viksit Bharat 2047. Despite rising acceptance of AI-based educational technology, equitable access, faculty preparedness, ethical governance, digital infrastructure, and curriculum revision for future workforce needs remain problems. This study critically investigates how AI and ML might improve the quality, accessibility, inclusivity, and effectiveness of higher education in India within NEP 2020. It examines the transformative potential of AI-enabled adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring, predictive learning analytics, automated assessment, academic administration, and research support, using a doctrinal and analytical research methodology grounded in policy documents, government reports, and contemporary academic literature. It also highlights algorithmic unfairness, data privacy, cybersecurity, digital inequality, academic integrity, and ethical issues in the implementation of generative AI. The Competency-Based AI Integration Framework (AI-HE 2047 Framework) integrates digital literacy, critical thinking, interdisciplinary learning, research and innovation, ethical AI governance, and lifelong learning competencies to align AI adoption with the goals of NEP 2020. The methodology helps higher education institutions produce AI-ready graduates for an innovation-driven knowledge economy. The study found that responsible integration of AI and ML, supported by policy reforms, faculty capacity building, institutional readiness, and ethical governance mechanisms, can improve educational quality, employability, research excellence, and India's transition to a knowledge-powered economy under Viksit Bharat 2047.

items.abstract: Abstract Patents Act drafted in 1970 for a world of mechanical assemblies and chemical formulations and then has to stretch them, sometimes uncomfortably, to fit technologies nobody anticipated. Artificial intelligence is the latest and perhaps the most demanding of these stretches. It is central to the country’s Viksit Bharat @2047 ambitions, driving growth in pharmaceuticals, semiconductor design, fintech, and advanced manufacturing, yet it sits awkwardly within a patent regime built on the presumption that an inventor is a natural person who can be named, questioned, and held accountable. This paper works through three points of friction between AI and Indian patent law, testing each against how comparable jurisdictions the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Patent Office have responded. The first is inventorship itself: whether a system such as DABUS can ever satisfy Sections 2(1)(y) and 6 of the Patents Act, 1970, and what happens to applications where a human contributor is named largely as a matter of convenience rather than genuine authorship. The second is the Section 3(k) exclusion for computer programmes per se and algorithms, read alongside the Delhi High Court’s technical-effect reasoning in Ferid Allani and its later application to AI-adjacent claims. The third concerns disclosure: what Section 10(4) can realistically demand of a model whose internal decision pathway is, by design, not fully interpretable even to the people who trained it. Rather than treat these as abstract doctrinal puzzles, the paper closes with a set of concrete, implementable proposals clarified guidance on human-contribution thresholds, an updated CRI examination manual with AI-specific illustrations, a Budapest-Treaty-style depository for training artefacts, and time-limited sui generis right for genuinely autonomous outputs. The underlying argument is a modest one: India does not need to choose between protecting human ingenuity and encouraging AI-driven research. It needs sharper definitions, and it needs them before the volume of AI-related filings makes ad hoc case-by-case resolution unworkable.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Academic Libraries: Advancing the Vision of Viksit Bharat@2047
items.abstract: Abstract The continuing advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is creating new possibilities for higher education and academic library development. The increasing volume of digital information, expansion of online education, and growing complexity of scholarly communication require libraries to provide faster, more responsive, and user-oriented information services. AI can assist academic libraries in areas such as intelligent discovery of scholarly resources, automated reference assistance, resource recommendation, metadata creation, research support, collection analysis, and digital preservation. This paper examines the emerging applications of AI in academic libraries and considers how these developments can support the broader objectives of Viksit Bharat@2047. Particular attention is given to the advantages of AI as well as concerns involving accuracy, privacy, copyright, ethics, infrastructure, digital inequality, and professional competencies. The paper argues that AI should function as an enabling technology rather than a substitute for librarians. The combination of computational capabilities with professional knowledge and human judgement can transform academic libraries into more responsive centres for learning, research, innovation, and knowledge sharing. Properly implemented AI-based library services can therefore strengthen the contribution of academic libraries to quality education, research capacity, digital literacy, and inclusive access to knowledge, thereby supporting India's long-term development aspirations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Human Resource Management: Building a Skilled Workforce for Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming Human Resource Management (HRM) through AI-enabled recruitment, workforce analytics, employee development, performance management and talent management. In the context of Viksit Bharat @2047, AI can play a significant role in developing a skilled, adaptable and future-ready workforce. This paper examines the role of AI in HRM and its contribution to workforce reskilling, digital literacy, analytical skills and human-AI collaboration. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research approach based on secondary literature, policy reports and an illustrative quantitative framework. The paper proposes an AI–HRM–Skills–Viksit Bharat framework, highlighting the importance of continuous learning, ethical AI governance and human-centred skills. It concludes that responsible integration of AI with effective reskilling and upskilling strategies can strengthen workforce productivity, employability, innovation and India's journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence For Climate-Resilient Plants: Emerging Ai Approaches For Predicting Drought, Salinity And Temperature Stress.
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change is creating serious problems for agriculture by increasing drought, soil salinity, and extreme temperatures. These stresses affect plant growth, development, crop yield, and global food security. Traditional methods used to study plant responses to stress are often time-consuming, labour-intensive, and difficult to use for large numbers of plants. Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an important tool for studying and predicting plant responses to changing environmental conditions. AI can analyse large amounts of data collected through plant phenotyping, remote sensing, environmental sensors, and molecular studies. This review focuses on recent AI approaches used to predict plant responses to drought, salinity, and temperature stress from 2016 to 2026. Machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, thermal imaging, and hyperspectral imaging can help in early detection and prediction of plant stress. Recent developments are moving beyond simple stress identification towards predicting crop performance and stress tolerance. The combination of AI with high-throughput phenotyping and multi-omics can help identify stress-tolerant crop varieties and support climate-resilient breeding. However, challenges related to data quality, limited field validation, unclear model predictions, and poor performance across different environments still remain. Future research should develop reliable and explainable AI models for sustainable agriculture and improved crop production under climate change.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable & Environmentally Benign Chemical Science
items.abstract: Abstract Green chemistry seeks to prevent pollution at its source by reducing waste, energy demand, hazardous substances, and resource consumption. Artificial intelligence (AI), especially machine learning (ML), can strengthen this approach by learning from chemical and process data, predicting outcomes, screening large chemical spaces, and optimizing experiments. Recent literature identifies applications ranging from catalyst discovery and reaction optimization to CO₂ capture, sustainable polymers, waste management, water treatment, and process control. A 2026 review in Applied Intelligence highlights artificial neural networks, random forests, and Bayesian optimization as important approaches across these areas, while also emphasizing data quality, validation, energy use, and scalability as major concerns. (see References 1–6) This project reviews how AI can support the principles of green chemistry and proposes a practical research framework in which sustainability metrics are included directly in model objectives. The central idea is that an AI system should not merely maximize chemical yield; it should seek a balanced outcome involving yield, selectivity, waste, toxicity, energy, solvent impact, and resource efficiency. The report concludes that AI can become an enabling technology for greener chemistry when models are transparent, experimentally validated, and evaluated against environmental as well as technical performance.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transitioning from a supportive tool to a core component of clinical decision-making in dentistry. This review synthesizes advances in deep learning and machine learning for oral disease diagnosis, orthodontic treatment prediction, pediatric oral health management, adolescent psychological-oral health interactions, and precision care for special-needs populations, drawing on evidence published predominantly between 2024 and 2026. A systematic search across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus identified 30 studies for narrative synthesis. Several AI models reported higher diagnostic or predictive performance than selected conventional comparators in detecting periodontal bone loss, temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis, and oral squamous cell carcinoma, with accuracy frequently exceeding 90%. In orthodontics, AI-driven prediction reduces tooth movement error rates substantially. However, most studies rely on single-center retrospective data lacking prospective multicenter validation. Future priorities include multimodal data fusion, federated learning, and standardized validation frameworks to facilitate clinical translation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Graphic Design: Exploring Creativity and Challenges
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly become part of contemporary visual communication and is changing the way graphic designers generate, develop, refine, and present ideas. Tools based on generative AI can produce images, illustrations, layouts, typography suggestions, visual variations, and creative concepts within seconds. For graphic designers, this development offers significant opportunities for experimentation and efficiency, but it also raises important questions about creativity, originality, authorship, professional identity, and the future of design education. This paper explores the relationship between artificial intelligence and graphic design from the perspective of creative practice. The paper argues that AI does not eliminate the need for human creativity; instead, it changes where creative effort takes place. Designers increasingly need to formulate problems, evaluate generated possibilities, make cultural and aesthetic judgments, refine outputs, and give visual communication a meaningful human direction. At the same time, excessive dependence on AI may lead to design fixation, visual similarity, weakened foundational skills, and uncertainty regarding authorship. The paper concludes that the most productive future for graphic design lies in responsible human–AI collaboration, supported by strong foundations in design principles, visual thinking, ethics, and critical judgment.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Interior Design: Opportunities, Challenges and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the design industry by introducing data-driven, generative, predictive, and automated approaches to creative and technical processes. Interior design, traditionally dependent on human creativity, spatial understanding, material knowledge, and client preferences, is increasingly influenced by AI-powered tools capable of generating design concepts, visualizations, layouts, material combinations, lighting solutions, and personalized spatial recommendations. Recent developments in generative AI, machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal systems have expanded the possibilities for designers to explore a larger number of alternatives in less time. This research paper examines the opportunities, challenges, and future perspectives associated with the integration of Artificial Intelligence into interior design. The study adopts a qualitative systematic literature review approach and synthesizes recent research on AI-assisted architectural and built-environment design. The review indicates that AI can support concept generation, space planning, 3D visualization, material selection, sustainability analysis, personalization, and client communication. However, issues related to creativity, algorithmic bias, intellectual property, data privacy, professional responsibility, design authenticity, technical skills, and overdependence on automated systems remain significant challenges. Recent systematic reviews show that AI research in design is strongly concentrated in early conceptual and schematic stages, while later stages requiring detailed technical, contextual, and professional judgment remain comparatively underexplored. The paper argues that AI should not be viewed as a replacement for interior designers but as an augmentation technology that can strengthen human creativity, decision-making, and productivity. A human-centred AI framework combining technological capability with professional expertise, ethical safeguards, cultural sensitivity, and user participation is proposed. The study concludes that the future of interior design will increasingly depend on effective human–AI collaboration rather than complete automation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Personal Finance Management: An Empirical Study of Young Investors in the Kalyan Region
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is embedded in every financial transaction and interaction through robo-advising, auto- Recommendations, portfolios tracking, digital financial assistants, and financial information processing tools. This paper considers the relevance of AI to young investors of the Kalyan Region. Using relevant published evidence from SEBI, NSE, AMFI and RBI, along with peer-reviewed research and analysis, this paper applies descriptive, comparative and trend-oriented analysis to examine the use and impact of AI in personal finance management. Evidence shows an ageing-down of India's investor base, with young people constituting an increasing proportion of the registered individual investors. The study finds that AI can reduce information and access barriers and enable personalisation, monitoring, and analysis. However, the benefits are limited by financial literacy, trust, perceived risk, transparency and ability to question AI outputs.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Chemistry: Applications, Challenges and Future Perspectives towards Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract The chemical industry is essential for modern society, but conventional chemical processes may require substantial quantities of energy, solvents and raw materials and can generate undesirable waste and emissions. Sustainable chemistry seeks to address these concerns by designing chemical products and processes that use resources more efficiently and reduce environmental and health risks. In parallel, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for analysing complex chemical information, predicting molecular and material properties, optimizing reactions and supporting scientific decision-making. The integration of AI with sustainable chemistry creates an opportunity to accelerate the development of safer, cleaner and more resource-efficient chemical technologies. This review examines the emerging role of AI in sustainable chemistry, with particular emphasis on machine learning, predictive modelling, reaction optimization, catalyst discovery, solvent selection, sustainable materials, carbon management, green hydrogen, waste valorization and analytical chemistry. The potential of AI to support the principles of green chemistry and life-cycle-based decision-making is also discussed. Recent studies indicate that AI can reduce experimental effort and improve the efficiency of chemical discovery and process development, although limitations related to data quality, interpretability, validation, computational requirements and industrial scale-up remain significant. The review further considers the relevance of AI-enabled sustainable chemistry to India's long-term development objectives under Viksit Bharat @2047. A future-oriented framework for responsible AI-driven chemistry is proposed, emphasizing scientific validation, environmental assessment, interdisciplinary collaboration and indigenous innovation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Advances in Analytical Chemistry: Methods, Applications, and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping analytical chemistry by changing how instrumental measurements are processed, interpreted, optimized, and translated into chemical decisions. Modern analytical platforms generate high-dimensional spectra, chromatograms, mass spectra, images, and sensor signals in volumes that can exceed the practical capacity of conventional univariate or manually supervised workflows. This integrative review examines AI-driven advances across spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), chemical sensors, imaging, and analytical method development. The review adopts a structured narrative design using purposive sampling of peer-reviewed reviews, primary methodological literature, and regulatory guidance identified through targeted searches of major biomedical and chemistry literature sources and official regulatory repositories. Evidence was thematically coded into four domains: data enhancement, predictive modelling, analytical-method optimization, and decision support. The synthesis indicates that machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), chemometrics, quantitative structure–retention relationships (QSRR), and hybrid mechanistic–data-driven approaches can improve pattern recognition, spectral deconvolution, analyte identification, retention prediction, calibration, anomaly detection, and experimental optimization when adequate and representative data are available. However, AI does not automatically create a valid analytical method: model leakage, biased sampling, poor external validation, instrument drift, explainability limitations, and weak uncertainty characterization can undermine apparent performance. Current regulatory thinking increasingly emphasizes risk-based credibility and conventional analytical validation principles. Future analytical laboratories are therefore likely to combine AI with robust metrology, automated experimentation, digital twins, explainable AI, multimodal data fusion, and continuous lifecycle validation. The central conclusion is that the strongest pathway is not replacement of analytical chemistry by AI, but integration of chemical knowledge, measurement science, and trustworthy computation.

items.title: Balancing the Books and the Backseat: Algorithmic Management, Student Gig Workers, and the Welfare Gap in India's AI-Driven Platform Economy under Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India's vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 rests significantly on harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) to power an inclusive digital economy, with the gig and platform sector projected to grow from 7.7 million workers in 2020-21 to 23.5 million by 2029-30 [1]. Within this expanding workforce lies an under-documented segment: college students who work as ride-hailing drivers and delivery partners for platforms such as Uber, Ola, Rapido, Swiggy, and Zomato alongside their academic commitments. While the Code on Social Security, 2020, operationalised through Rules notified in 2025-26, extends formal welfare recognition to gig and platform workers for the first time, it remains largely silent on the algorithmic mechanisms, dynamic pricing, rating-based deactivation, and automated task allocation, that govern their day-to-day work experience, a gap well documented in the international algorithmic-management literature [2], [3], [4]. This paper examines the intersection of AI-driven algorithmic management and worker welfare policy through a mixed-methods approach: a review of the current regulatory framework combined with primary survey data (n = 18) collected from college students in Coimbatore district engaged in gig work. The findings show that a majority of respondents report unpredictable pricing (70.6%) and roughly two in five report unfair ratings (41.2%) or deactivation/suspension (35.3%), while awareness of the e-Shram portal (52.9%) and of statutory welfare benefits (58.8%, with a further 23.5% only vaguely aware) remains partial. items.title: Balancing the Books and the Backseat: Algorithmic Management, Student Gig Workers, and the Welfare Gap in India's AI-Driven Platform Economy under Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India's vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 rests significantly on harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) to power an inclusive digital economy, with the gig and platform sector projected to grow from 7.7 million workers in 2020-21 to 23.5 million by 2029-30 [1]. Within this expanding workforce lies an under-documented segment: college students who work as ride-hailing drivers and delivery partners for platforms such as Uber, Ola, Rapido, Swiggy, and Zomato alongside their academic commitments. While the Code on Social Security, 2020, operationalised through Rules notified in 2025-26, extends formal welfare recognition to gig and platform workers for the first time, it remains largely silent on the algorithmic mechanisms, dynamic pricing, rating-based deactivation, and automated task allocation, that govern their day-to-day work experience, a gap well documented in the international algorithmic-management literature [2], [3], [4]. This paper examines the intersection of AI-driven algorithmic management and worker welfare policy through a mixed-methods approach: a review of the current regulatory framework combined with primary survey data (n = 18) collected from college students in Coimbatore district engaged in gig work. The findings show that a majority of respondents report unpredictable pricing (70.6%) and roughly two in five report unfair ratings (41.2%) or deactivation/suspension (35.3%), while awareness of the e-Shram portal (52.9%) and of statutory welfare benefits (58.8%, with a further 23.5% only vaguely aware) remains partial. The paper concludes with a policy framework recommending algorithmic transparency mandates, accessible grievance redressal mechanisms, and targeted awareness measures for student and youth gig workers, contributing to the broader goal of inclusive, technology-driven, and socially secure economic growth envisioned under Viksit Bharat @2047.

items.title: Bots Behaving Badly: The implications of bot traffic on research and knowledge in the AI economy
items.abstract: Most academic and nonprofit institutions have mission- and policy-driven mandates to make research data publicly available at no cost to users, however the viability of maintaining “open access,” public collections in the rapidly developing AI ecosystem is uncertain. Since 2022, rising bot traffic associated with large language models and machine learning has cost research collection hosts and maintainers increasing amounts of time, labor, and money. Academic institutions, data hubs, and open collections like Wikipedia all report struggles to minimize downtime and compute costs due to bot confrontations. While defense against bots is an urgent, visceral concern right now, collections managers in these institutions have a particular existential concern: that the bot traffic signifies that entrepreneurial technologists are absorbing generations of curatorial work into systems that may ultimately undermine those collections. This concern is exacerbated by the difficulty in gauging collection “use” (and therefore, value) by traditional website analytics and metrics. What if these challenges, taken together, could also signify opportunities - including mechanisms to encourage better behavior from bots? Our poster will share findings regarding current approaches taken by collection curators. We will then share several new approaches that explicitly work to shift both technical and social incentives in order to address these issues.

items.title: Bridging the Education–Employment Gap under NEP 2020: AI Literacy, Communication Competence, and Work-Integrated Learning for Graduate Employability
items.abstract: Abstract India's expansion of higher education has created unprecedented opportunities for young people, yet the movement from educational qualification to meaningful employment remains uneven. The central challenge is no longer simply access to degrees but the relationship between credentials, capabilities, workplace experience, and employment outcomes. This conceptual paper examines how the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 can contribute to narrowing this education–employment gap through the integrated development of AI literacy, communication competence, and work-integrated learning. Drawing on recent policy evidence from NITI Aayog, the International Labour Organization, and contemporary scholarship on artificial intelligence and work-integrated learning, the paper argues that employability should not be treated as an additional soft-skills component appended to an academic curriculum. Rather, it should emerge from a coherent educational architecture connecting disciplinary knowledge with communication, digital and AI capabilities, authentic workplace exposure, critical thinking, and demonstrable competence. The paper proposes an integrated framework in which AI literacy and communication competence function as enabling capabilities, while work-integrated learning provides the context in which those capabilities are tested and developed. It concludes by suggesting institutional measures through which Indian higher education can move from credential-centred education towards competency-, experience-, and outcome-oriented graduate preparation.

items.title: ChatGPT, Achievement Motivation, and Problem-Solving: Evidence from Thai and Cambodian Undergraduates
items.abstract: Background. The rapid global adoption of ChatGPT has raised growing interest in its role in supporting student learning, yet the effectiveness of generative AI tools in enhancing higher-order cognitive skills such as problem-solving may depend on individual learner characteristics that remain underexplored. Purpose. This quantitative study aimed to examine the relationship between ChatGPT usage and problem-solving ability among students enrolled in a Media Design course, and to test whether this relationship is moderated by achievement motivation. Method. The study involved 115 university students from four intact classes across two higher education institutions in Thailand and Cambodia. Data were collected through a survey questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), preceded by a measurement invariance test (MICOM) to assess the appropriateness of pooling data across the two national samples. Results. The findings indicate that ChatGPT usage was positively and significantly associated with problem-solving ability (? = 0.386, p < 0.001), as was achievement motivation (? = 0.291, p < 0.01). The interaction between ChatGPT usage and achievement motivation also showed a significant positive effect (? = 0.157, p < 0.05), indicating that achievement motivation strengthens the relationship between ChatGPT usage and problem-solving ability. The model explained 44.6% of the variance in problem-solving ability (R² = 0.446). Conclusion. This study has significant implications for instructional practices in higher education settings, particularly for lecturers designing AI-integrated learning activities. By understanding how achievement motivation shapes students’ benefit from ChatGPT, educators can tailor instructional strategies that support both technology adoption and the development of independent problem solving skills.
