items.title: Computer Vision System and Transformer-Based Multimodal Fusion of Medical Images for Enhanced Diagnostic Decision Making
items.abstract: The rise of artificial intelligence technologies and their increasing reliance in numerous fields, most notably medicine, is significant. AI plays a crucial role in assisting physicians with accurate patient diagnosis, enabling them to make informed decisions. This article presents a method for integrating computer vision technologies into the medical field, where multimodal medical imaging integrates structural and textual information to support clinical decision-making. However, most image fusion frameworks based on transformers remain narrowly designed for a single media combination and a single subsequent task. This paper proposes the Multimodal Adaptive Fusion Transformer (CMAFT), a unified architecture that combines Swin transformer encoders for each media with a Catalyst Cross Attention Fusion Module (GCAF) to dynamically weight each media's contribution based on its real-time reliability. CMAFT was evaluated against two structurally different multimodal reference standards: the BraTS 2021 dataset, in which four MRI sequences (T1, T1ce, T2, FLAIR) were combined to segment brain tumor volumes, and the MIMIC-CXR dataset, in which chest X-ray images were combined with duplex radiology report inclusions to classify multimodal pathology and generate reports. The proposed GCAF module provides a learnable reliability gateway that curbs degraded or lost data streams, while a multiscale hierarchical integration pyramid preserves both fine detail and overall semantic context. Experiments show that CMAFT achieves average Dice scores of 92.4%, 87.9%, and 84.6% for whole tumor, tumor nucleus, and enhanced tumor, respectively, on the BraTS 2021 dataset, and a multi-class average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.876 with an overall F1 value of 0.658 on the MIMIC-CXR dataset, outperforming modern hybrid CNN-Transformer models while using fewer parameters compared to similar dual-code baseline models. Resection studies confirm that both reliability gate and multi-scale integration contribute to measurable gains, and that CMAFT degrades smoothly when either an MRI sequence or radiology report is unavailable. These results suggest that a single adaptive mutual attention integration design can be generalized across volumetric and text-based multimodal diagnostic pathways.

items.title: Death of Human Style of Writing in the World of AI
items.abstract: Abstract: The Artificial Intelligence (AI) writing tools like ChatGPT and Claude have changed the world of official and unofficial communication in last two to three years. The human style of writing is diminishing and there is a rise of only one universal writing style created by the AI tools which lack human expressions and creativity. The AI tools are rampantly used by students, researchers, writers and people in general for any kind of serious as well as casual writing today. The excessive use of AI tools in writing is also responsible for reducing human ability of logical and critical thinking. Therefore, there is an urgency of using AI writing tools wisely so that the human writing skills get enhanced and the tools prove to be a boon. This research paper examines the challenges posed by AI writing tools and discusses how the AI can be used effectively and responsibly to enhance human writing skills.

items.title: Death of Human Style of Writing in the World of AI
items.abstract: Abstract: The Artificial Intelligence (AI) writing tools like ChatGPT and Claude have changed the world of official and unofficial communication in last two to three years. The human style of writing is diminishing and there is a rise of only one universal writing style created by the AI tools which lack human expressions and creativity. The AI tools are rampantly used by students, researchers, writers and people in general for any kind of serious as well as casual writing today. The excessive use of AI tools in writing is also responsible for reducing human ability of logical and critical thinking. Therefore, there is an urgency of using AI writing tools wisely so that the human writing skills get enhanced and the tools prove to be a boon. This research paper examines the challenges posed by AI writing tools and discusses how the AI can be used effectively and responsibly to enhance human writing skills.

items.title: Decoding the 'Viksit' Consumer: Integrating AI, Smart Technologies, and Asset Lifecycle Theories for Sustainable Development towards Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract With the country working towards the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, the way we look at technology, sustainability, and market trends is seeing a major change. While we often label the Indian buyer as strictly price-sensitive, today’s consumer is actually quite digital and eco-conscious. However, there is still a mental block when it comes to investing in expensive green technology. People worry about the product losing its value or becoming outdated too quickly—a classic case of 'asset depreciation' in accounting terms, which in everyday life simply translates to a fear of losing 'value for money'. The present study explores how Artificial Intelligence and smart tools are helping brands reshape their marketing to overcome this hesitation. Based on a detailed review of secondary data, we examine how AI-based personalisation, local language (vernacular) interfaces, and circular economy models are changing buying habits across both urban 'India' and rural 'Bharat'. By connecting traditional accounting concepts with modern marketing strategies, the findings show that smart technologies are doing much more than just driving sales. They are actively helping to build genuine consumer trust and encouraging sustainable buying habits, which is exactly what is needed to achieve our national development goals for 2047.

items.title: Developments in the Field of Photography and the Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Smart Technologies in a Developed India
items.abstract: Abstract Developments in the field of photography and the contribution of artificial intelligence have been remarkable in a developing India. The journey from early optical and chemical processes to digital visual communication has been significant. Technologies ranging from everyday applications to film, digital photography, smart photography, cloud platforms, machine learning, generative AI, drones, and IoT devices (such as Alexa) have vastly expanded the possibilities for capturing, processing, interpreting, and sharing images. Modern photography is no longer limited to just cameras, lenses, digital sensors, and photographers; smart technologies are increasingly playing a pivotal role in processes such as focusing, exposure, color correction, noise reduction, dynamic range enhancement, subject recognition, image segmentation, autofocus, image enhancement, and post-production. Research into AI and photography indicates that machine learning and computational processing have transformed the traditional boundaries between image capture and image processing. In India, these changes are unfolding within a digital framework. The Government of India’s 'IndiaAI' mission received approval in March 2024, aiming to strengthen computing infrastructure, data availability, AI innovation, and world-class development. This emerging technology ecosystem directly impacts photography and visual media education, as well as professional fields such as journalism, advertising, fashion product imaging, scientific documentation, wildlife and heritage conservation, and the creative industries. Furthermore, generative AI is driving a profound transformation; images can now be enhanced, recreated, modified, or generated from scratch without every visible element being directly linked to an optical phenomenon. This opens up new creative opportunities. However, issues regarding authenticity, the author's copyright, privacy, consent, employment, cultural representation, and public trust also arise. This research paper examines the historical evolution of photography, the opportunities for India in the field of photography alongside smart technology, the challenges faced by photographers and educators, and a proposed framework for responsible photography in a developing India.

items.title: Digital Competence of Preservice Primary School Teachers: The Role of Digital Material Development Experience and Self-Assessed Artificial Intelligence Use Competence
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the digital competence levels of preservice primary school teachers, examine whether their competence differed according to personal and experiential variables, and investigate the relationship between self-assessed artificial intelligence (AI) use competence and digital competence. The study employed descriptive and correlational survey designs with 119 preservice teachers enrolled in primary school teacher education programs at five universities. Data were collected through a Personal Information Form, which included a single-item self-assessment of AI use competence, and the 25-item, five-dimensional Teacher Digital Competence Scale. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression were used. Overall digital competence was high. Scores did not differ significantly by gender, age, year of study, previous digital technology training, or previous AI training. Participants with digital material development experience had significantly higher competence (Hedges’ g = 0.76). Self-assessed AI use competence was strongly and positively associated with overall digital competence (r = .646) and accounted for 41.7% of its variance. The findings suggest that active digital production and AI-supported material development experiences are associated with stronger digital competence and deserve attention in teacher education.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Municipal Corporations in India: Opportunities and Challenges for Achieving the Viksit Bharat 2047 Vision
items.abstract: Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 seeks to transform the country into a developed nation by the centenary of independence. Municipal corporations have a central role in this transformation because the quality of urban governance directly affects citizens’ everyday lives, economic activity, environmental sustainability and social well-being. Rapid urbanisation, increasing demand for public services, climate-related risks and growing expectations for transparent administration have created a need for municipal institutions to adopt digital technologies. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the digital transformation of municipal corporations in India. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, geographic information systems, cloud computing, digital payment systems, data analytics, Internet of Things applications and online citizen-service platforms can improve municipal administration. Particular attention is given to digital revenue collection, solid-waste management, water and sanitation services, urban planning, grievance redressal, traffic management and citizen participation. The paper argues that digital transformation should not be understood merely as the computerisation of existing municipal processes. Instead, it should involve institutional reform, data-driven decision-making, inclusive service delivery, employee capacity building, cybersecurity and sustainable urban development. At the same time, municipalities face challenges including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, shortage of skilled personnel, fragmented databases, cybersecurity risks, unequal access to technology and resistance to organisational change. The paper proposes a citizen-centric and sustainable digital governance framework through which municipal corporations can contribute meaningfully to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Teacher Education under Vikshit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India's vision of Vikshit Bharat @2047 rests on building a digitally empowered, innovation-driven, and sustainable economy in which artificial intelligence, e-commerce, and digital infrastructure serve as engines of inclusive growth. Realising this vision depends critically on the quality of human capital that education systems produce, and teacher education stands at the centre of that pipeline. This paper examines how the digital transformation envisaged under Vikshit Bharat @2047 is reshaping teacher education in India, using the reforms introduced under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 as the entry point. It discusses how national digital platforms such as DIKSHA, SWAYAM, and PM eVIDYA, together with emerging technologies including artificial intelligence, virtual and augmented reality, blockchain, and the Internet of Things, are creating new possibilities for personalised, inclusive, and lifelong teacher development. The paper also situates these developments within the wider digital economy, arguing that a technologically competent teaching workforce is a precondition for the commerce, innovation, and productivity gains that Vikshit Bharat @2047 anticipates. At the same time, the paper identifies significant risks, including the digital divide, uneven digital literacy among teachers, and adverse effects of excessive technology use on mental well-being, sleep, and attention. Drawing on secondary literature and policy documents, the paper proposes a blended and sustainability-oriented framework for teacher education that combines digital tools with face-to-face mentoring, structured digital wellness training, and continuous monitoring of technology use. It concludes that India's digital future will be strongest where digital ambition is matched with digital responsibility, and where teacher education is treated as strategic national infrastructure rather than a peripheral concern.

items.title: DPMF: A Dynamic Risk-Aware Permission Framework for Securing AI Agents Using Third-Party APIs
items.abstract: AI agents are moving from systems that only generate information to systems that can plan tasks, use tools, and perform operations through external APIs. This shift creates a security problem that traditional permission models do not fully address: an agent may hold broad privileges even when a particular task needs only a small part of that access. A valid token therefore does not automatically mean that every action produced by the agent is appropriate. This paper proposes DPMF (Dynamic Risk-Aware Permission Framework), an external authorization layer for AI agents that interact with third-party services. DPMF evaluates each proposed API action using contextual signals such as user-intent alignment, data sensitivity, permission severity, source trust, action reversibility, and behavioral deviation. The resulting risk level drives one of four decisions: Allow, Restrict, Human Approval, or Deny. The framework also separates the agent's ability to propose an action from the security layer's authority to approve it. The paper presents the framework architecture, threat model, risk-scoring approach, dynamic permission algorithm, case study, and an experimental methodology for comparing DPMF with static authorization. Because the framework has not yet been experimentally implemented, no numerical performance claims are presented as established results. Instead, measurable evaluation criteria and expected outcomes are defined.
